report:
### Conclusion
The health claim is **true**. Strong clinical evidence demonstrates that initiating tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) during the third trimester (around 28 weeks' gestation) in pregnant women with chronic hepatitis B virus (HBV) and high viral load significantly reduces mother-to-child (perinatal) transmission when added to standard infant immunoprophylaxis (vaccine and hepatitis B immune globulin).

### Key Evidence
* **Clinical Trials:** A landmark randomized controlled trial by Pan et al. demonstrated that maternal TDF treatment starting in the third trimester rapidly reduced maternal viral load before delivery, significantly lowering perinatal HBV transmission compared to standard care alone.
* **Systematic Reviews:** Meta-analyses confirm that third-trimester TDF prophylaxis substantially lowers maternal HBV DNA levels, decreases transmission risk, and exhibits a favorable safety profile with no significant adverse maternal or fetal outcomes.
* **Global Guidelines:** The World Health Organization (WHO) and major international hepatology associations recommend TDF prophylaxis starting at 28 weeks' gestation for HBsAg-positive pregnant women with high HBV DNA ($\ge 200,000\text{ IU/mL}$) or positive HBeAg status.

### Sources
1. **WHO PMTCT Guidelines:** https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/978-92-4-000270-8
2. **Third-trimester Tenofovir Clinical Trial Overview:** https://ijmr.org.in/third-trimester-tenofovir-to-prevent-mother-to-child-hepatitis-b-virus-transmission/
3. **Systematic Review on TDF Efficacy:** https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/41345578/
4. **WHO 2024 Guidelines Update (The Lancet):** https://www.thelancet.com/journals/langas/article/PIIS2468-1253(24)00089-X/fulltext
